ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution with approximately 75% high-intensity (white) pixels and 25% low-intensity (black) pixels localized primarily at the trailing edge and median base.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white geometric regions cover the central and lower portions of both lobes; dark pigment mottling is concentrated along the trailing edge and in a dense cluster surrounding the median notch; numerous small, dark focal points (circular) are scattered throughout the white zones.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with a calculated angle of approximately 60 degrees; lower vertex of the notch is partially obscured by water spray.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular pixel-amplitude variations across the entire trailing edge; extreme ruggedness and deep valley-peak transitions visible on the outer terminal end of the right lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Trailing edges exhibit a strong convex curve tapering towards the tips; leading edges show a concave curve partially submerged in the water plane.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple dark, circular pixel clusters (annular rosettes) ranging from 5-15 pixels in diameter scattered across both lobes, likely indicating barnacle attachment sites.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Numerous unaligned, dark linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) crossing the white ventral surface, most prominently visible as diagonal and vertical strikes on the lower left and upper right lobes.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Heavy biological/calcified accumulation on the distal tips of both lobes creating a jagged, high-contrast silhouette; a significant irregular traumatic indentation is visible on the inner-upper trailing edge of the right lobe.
other_distinctive_markers: Asymmetric serration pattern where the right fluke tip displays significantly more jagged, protruding topographical features compared to the relatively smoother (though still serrated) left tip.
